An AI experiment on an island inside a computer showed how much these strategy notes can matter.

primary.label: SECONDARY_ASR_CORROBORATED_MATCH

primary.text: Then one AI started an obstacle course of its own. It surrounded a building called the cathedral with eight blocks and jumped across without touching the ground. It designed the course and made the rules all by itself. It was keeping pretty busy, even though nobody had asked it to. The researchers say this shows a feature of play.
primary.label: NUMERIC_EQUIVALENCE_MATCH

primary.text: But the jumps were not the only thing worth watching. In the experiment, the island and the conversation were reset every hour, but the work area where the AI kept notes and programs was carried over. The island went back to how it was before, but what the AI had discovered was not erased.
primary.label: EXACT_MATCH

primary.text: So, would that experience help the AI the next time it was called on? The researchers compared 13 AIs that had experience on the island with 13 AIs that had the same setup, but no such experience. On a new island, the challenge was to build as many towers as possible, each five blocks high, in one hour. When the researchers looked at whether the AIs could build more than two, the experienced group did better. The ones that had taken a detour were now one step ahead.
primary.label: NORMALIZED_MATCH

primary.text: The researchers also removed a description of a technique for throwing rocks to get more blocks from one AI's memory. After that, the average number of towers it could build fell. Its scores on other tasks did not change. At least for this AI, remembering that technique helped it build towers. One tip in the strategy notes was not something to overlook.
primary.label: NUMERIC_EQUIVALENCE_MATCH

primary.text: Even so, it is too soon to wave a flag and say, play and get smarter, proof complete. The fact that the experienced group did better and the fact that removing a particular memory lowered its score need to be looked at separately. These results alone do not show that play itself had an effect.
primary.label: NORMALIZED_MATCH

primary.text: Still, this changes how we see a detour. A discovery that is no use right now might become a useful card to play next time, if it is saved. If you see an AI jumping around on the island, pay attention to its notes as well as its feet. Its next hour might depend on a discovery written down in just one line.
primary.label: TRUE_CONTENT_MISMATCH
